title: High-Threshold Fusion-Based Quantum Computation with Optical Hybrid Qubits
authors: Seong-Yeop Lim, Jaehak Lee, Nuri Kang, Seung-Woo Lee
abstract: Hybrid discrete- and continuous-variable (DV-CV) encodings have been developed to overcome operational drawbacks of each individual encoding, while fusion-based quantum computation (FBQC) has emerged to address the practical challenges of scalability toward fault-tolerant photonic quantum computation. Here we introduce hybrid FBQC using small optical DV-CV hybrid resource states connected through hybrid fusions, to combine the advantages of both approaches. We develop protocols for directly generating these resource states without requiring local hybrid logic such as the Hadamard gate, together with a tailored decoding strategy that exploits the error information contained in individual hybrid-fusion outcomes. We demonstrate that hybrid FBQC achieves a photon loss threshold of 2.231% while requiring only 12 hybrid fusions per surface-code unit cell, substantially improving upon the 0.89% threshold and 60-fusion requirement of previous hybrid measurement-based scheme. These results establish optical hybrid FBQC as a high-threshold resource-efficient route to scalable fault-tolerant photonic quantum computation.
summary: This paper introduces a novel hybrid approach to fault-tolerant photonic quantum computation by combining discrete-variable and continuous-variable quantum encoding within a fusion-based framework. By developing protocols for direct resource state generation and using outcome-aware decoding, the authors significantly improve the fault-tolerance threshold and reduce the required physical resources compared to previous hybrid schemes.
main_problem: To develop a scalable, fault-tolerant photonic quantum computation scheme that effectively combines the advantages of discrete-variable (DV) and continuous-variable (CV) quantum encodings.
main_result: The proposed hybrid fusion-based quantum computation (FBQC) achieves a significantly improved photon loss threshold of 2.231% while requiring only 12 hybrid fusions per surface-code unit cell.
method: The authors developed protocols for directly generating hybrid resource states and employing an outcome-aware decoding strategy that processes error information from individual hybrid-fusion outcomes.
model_or_system: The system utilizes optical hybrid qubits combining single-photon polarization (DV) and coherent/cat-code states (CV). Computation is performed via fusion measurements on these hybrid resource states, forming a surface code structure.
key_observables: Photon loss threshold ($\eta$), number of hybrid fusions required per unit cell, and conditional error probabilities ($p_{	ext{ZZ}}, p_{	ext{XX}}$).
important_parameters: The CV-state amplitude ($\alpha$) is a key parameter influencing the threshold; the resource cost is measured by the number of required fusion operations.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes independent loss channels with a constant loss rate ($\eta$) and relies on the ability to assign outcome-conditioned error probabilities based on measurement records.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the optical hybrid FBQC architecture, showing the unit cell structure, and detail the direct resource state preparation circuits for 4-Star and 6-Ring networks.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the hybrid encoding and the FBQC framework, then detailing the direct resource state generation protocols, followed by a rigorous error analysis using outcome-aware decoding, culminating in the quantitative demonstration of the improved threshold and resource efficiency.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems as it proposes a concrete, resource-efficient pathway for fault-tolerant computation using photonic platforms, directly addressing scalability challenges in quantum information processing.
